title: People’s Mañanera October 30
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Taddei Entered the INE Through a Random Selection Process in 2023, Not
Through Appointment by Any Political Party  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum rejected impunity in the case of recently
resigned National Electoral Institute (INE) president Guadalupe Taddei and
demanded an audit of INE and Local Electoral Bodies (OPLE) contracts. Such
contracts have been concentrated in two companies since 1999 due to
institutional practices that promoted such behavior. She recalled that the INE
president was elected by random selection because there was no agreement among
the parties regarding a specific candidate profile. A video was shown of past
INE president Lorenzo Córdova acknowledging the existence of the duopoly and
stating that the Council he headed appointed Taddei to the Sonora OPLE in
2014.

**Day of the Dead: The Pride of Being Mexican  
** “Our vision comes from the Indigenous peoples,” Sheinbaum affirmed. The
President noted that today 90% of the country’s citizens feel proud to be
Mexican, in contrast to the erosion of identity during the neoliberal era.

**From the 1988 Election Fraud to a Democracy Where the People Rule  
** Sheinbaum recalled that Cárdenas was robbed of his victory at the polls and
defended the freedoms won by the people. The President criticized right-wing
intellectuals Enrique Krauze and Héctor Aguilar Camín for longing for their
checks and privileges. “We don’t buy people’s support. We are building a
democratic country,” she explained.

**40 Years of the CEU: The Power of Reason in Defense of the UNAM  
** The President recalled that the student movement, led by the University
Student Council (CEU), in which she participated, democratically educated tens
of thousands of young people. She championed dialogue, public debate, and
reasoned arguments as tools to defend the university.
